speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are presenting with postpartum fever and abdominal tenderness; to help me narrow down the cause, how many days postpartum are you, and are you currently breastfeeding? Additionally, have you noticed any foul-smelling discharge from the uterus or pain when moving your bowels?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Peritonitis secondary to Postpartum Enterocutaneous Fistula or Ruptured Viscus.

The patient reports decreased bowel sounds and uterine tenderness after a difficult, prolonged labor with an 11-pound infant, which raises concern for visceral injury or perforation rather than standard puerperal infection. Have you experienced any episodes of vomiting or visible abdominal distension since delivery? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CXR_and_Abdominal_CT_with_contrast.
